name: Bierlachs
summary: A beer-stake variant of Skat where only minus points count and the first to hit a target loses and pays.
rules_text: Bierlachs is played with the full rules of three- or four-handed Skat including bidding for declarer and trick-taking. Before play a losing target is agreed, typically 301, 401 or 501 points, sometimes plus the calendar date. Scoring is negative only. If declarer wins a deal worth e.g. 40, each opponent receives -40. If declarer loses, declarer receives double, e.g. -80, opponents receive nothing for that deal. Cumulative minus scores are kept. As soon as a player reaches or exceeds the target in the negative direction, the session ends, that player is the overall loser and pays for a round of beer or pays into the Skat pot. Then a new session may start.
rating_reason: Skat variant race to points, trick-taking strategic game.
